definitions.gloss: poor at, weak in, not good at
definitions.explanation: Lacking skill or ability in something; finding something difficult.
Finding a person or thing difficult to handle or uncomfortable to be around.

examples.japanese: {数学|すうがく}が{苦手|にがて}です。
{朝|あさ}{起|お}きるのが{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: I'm bad at waking up early.

examples.japanese: {苦手|にがて}な{食|た}べ{物|もの}はありますか。
examples.english: Is there any food you don't like?

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{苦手|にがて}なタイプの{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He's the type of person I find difficult to deal with.

examples.japanese: {虫|むし}が{苦手|にがて}で、{見|み}るだけで{怖|こわ}い。
examples.english: I can't handle bugs — just seeing them scares me.

examples.japanese: {苦手|にがて}な{上司|じょうし}がいると、{毎日|まいにち}の{仕事|しごと}がつらくなる。
examples.english: When you have a boss you don't get along with, everyday work becomes tough.

notes:
USAGE: {苦手|にがて} is the opposite of {得意|とくい}. It's used to express weakness in skills or discomfort with people/situations.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜が{苦手|にがて}だ (to be poor at ~)
・{苦手|にがて}な{科目|かもく} (weak subject)
・{苦手|にがて}な{人|ひと} (person one finds hard to deal with)
・{苦手|にがて}を{克服|こくふく}する (to overcome a weakness)
・{苦手|にがて}{意識|いしき} (feeling of inadequacy)

NUANCE: {苦手|にがて} is a softer way to say you're bad at something compared to {下手|へた} (unskillful). It suggests personal difficulty rather than objective lack of skill.

ANTONYM:
・{得意|とくい} (good at, specialty)
